patients.summary: Retired construction foreman with COPD on home oxygen, metastatic non-small cell lung cancer under outside oncology, and prior DVT with post-thrombotic syndrome on warfarin. Joins in 2021, quits smoking in 2022, then has a run of postoperative and thrombotic emergencies (wound dehiscence, three pulmonary emboli, two hypercapnic COPD admissions) and a cardiac tamponade after his last practice visit. Outside records reach the practice unevenly.

documents.title: New patient scheduling call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Wife phoned on his behalf. Their old doctor retired and they heard about the membership model from a neighbor. He has lung cancer treated at an outside oncology office and is on oxygen at home, takes warfarin. Booked a 60 minute new patient slot 8/24 at 9:00. Asked her to bring all pill bottles and the oxygen company's name. Membership packet emailed. Records release form sent for the prior primary care office.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, high MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
66M here with his wife to establish. Previous PCP retired this summer.

PULM: COPD for years, on continuous O2 2 L by cannula since 2018; followed by an outside pulmonology group, who keep him on tiotropium daily, albuterol as needed and prednisone 5 mg daily as a maintenance dose. Walks the driveway and around the house with the portable concentrator. No hospital stays for his lungs in the past year by his account.

ONC: Lung cancer found Nov 2020 at an outside oncology group, already spread at diagnosis (non-small cell). Port placed then. Had chemo plus immunotherapy, now on pembrolizumab every 3 weeks through the port. Says the last scan was 'holding steady.' Tolerating it.

HEME: Leg clot 2019, has stayed on warfarin since, goal 2-3. Leg aches and feels heavy by evening, wears knee-high stockings most days (post-thrombotic). INRs had been done at the old office; would like us to take that over.

HTN on amlodipine 10.

TOBACCO: still smoking, about half a pack a day, down from much more; 40 pack-years. We talked plainly about cigarettes and oxygen in the same room. He knows. Not ready to set a date yet but willing to talk again.
Alcohol a drink or two a week. Retired construction foreman. Lives with wife.
FHx: father lung cancer, mother COPD, brother had a DVT.
NKDA.

Exam: thin, pleasant, nasal cannula in place, speaking full sentences. BP and SpO2 as charted on 2 L. Lungs: distant breath sounds, prolonged expiration, no crackles. Heart regular. Port right upper chest, clean. Legs: compression stockings on; no pitting today, mild brownish skin change at the ankles.

A/P
- COPD/chronic hypoxemic resp failure on home O2: continue regimen; pulm to keep managing.
- Metastatic NSCLC: per oncology; will request their notes.
- Hx DVT with PTS on warfarin: we will manage INR, nurse visit monthly to start. INR today.
- HTN: fine today, continue.
- Tobacco: revisit at each visit.
- Labs today, HCV and HIV once. Prior PCP records requested.
Back in ~3 months; INR check in 4 weeks.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Howard, everything from Tuesday came back fine: kidney and liver tests, blood counts, cholesterol all reasonable. INR was 2.4, right where we want it, so stay on 5 mg daily. Hep C and HIV screens negative. Our nurse will see you in about four weeks for the next INR.

documents.title: Records from prior primary care office
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Received by fax, 46 pages, covering 2015-2021 from his former primary care office. Highlights abstracted for PCP:
- Colonoscopy 2017: normal, no polyps.
- Left over to us: DVT treated 2019, warfarin indefinitely; INR log through June 2021, mostly 2-3.
- COPD, home oxygen ordered 2018.
- Hypertension on amlodipine 10 mg.
- Lung cancer diagnosed Nov 2020, care at oncology.
- Immunizations: influenza yearly; two COVID mRNA doses spring 2021; no pneumococcal conjugate on file; no Shingrix; last tetanus 2010.
Filed to media.

documents.title: Anticoagulation nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for INR. No bleeding, no bruising beyond usual, no missed doses, no new meds. Diet unchanged. Result in range, continue warfarin 5 mg every day. Next check in 4 weeks, booked.

documents.title: Oncology progress letter
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology group — letter to new primary care physician, visit of 9/2/2021.

Mr. Finn is a 66-year-old man with stage IV non-small cell lung cancer diagnosed November 2020. Implanted port placed at diagnosis. He received four cycles of carboplatin, pemetrexed and pembrolizumab and has continued on pembrolizumab maintenance every three weeks. Restaging CT chest, abdomen and pelvis in August shows stable disease without new lesions. Tolerating treatment without immune-related toxicity; thyroid and liver tests normal on our labs.

Other: COPD on 2 L home oxygen, prednisone 5 mg daily, warfarin for prior DVT. Allergies: NKDA.

Plan: continue pembrolizumab every 3 weeks; port flushed with each infusion; CT every 3 months. We strongly support smoking cessation.

Thank you for sharing his care.

documents.title: INR and flu vaccine
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR drawn, in goal. No bleeding. Same dose. High-dose flu given left deltoid, tolerated, VIS given. Oncology aware he is getting flu shot (pt asked them last week, ok with immunotherapy). Next INR 4-5 wks, ties in with his 11/16 visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Doing about the same. Breathing at baseline, using albuterol once or twice a day, more on cold mornings. Getting pembrolizumab q3wk, oncology says scans stable. Legs ache in the evenings, stockings help. Still smoking, ~8-10 a day. Says his wife wants him to quit more than he does. We spent a few minutes on what has worked for others; he'll think about patch vs. medication.

O: Vitals reviewed. Cannula on 2 L. Breath sounds diminished throughout, no wheeze today. RRR. No leg edema with stockings.

A/P:
1. COPD on home O2 - stable. Continue.
2. NSCLC - per onc.
3. Warfarin/hx DVT - INR today; monthly RN checks working well.
4. HTN - acceptable.
5. Tobacco - pre-contemplative-to-contemplative. Revisit in Feb.
6. Vaccines: PCV20 today, COVID booster today.
RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Anticoagulation nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR check. Reports no bleeding, no falls. Holiday eating coming up; reviewed keeping greens steady rather than cutting them out. In range, no change. Return mid-January.

documents.title: INR slightly low
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR a little under goal today. He thinks he may have skipped a dose over New Year's. No new meds, no antibiotics. Per PCP standing protocol: take 7.5 mg (1.5 tabs) tonight only, then resume 5 mg daily. Recheck 2 weeks. Pt repeated back instructions.

documents.title: INR recheck reminder
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Called to remind of INR recheck tomorrow. Spoke with wife, she will bring him.

documents.title: INR recheck
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Back in range. 5 mg daily. Seeing PCP 2/15, will do next INR with that visit if due, otherwise March.

medications.sig: Apply 1 patch to skin daily; remove old patch

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up / tobacco
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Came in today saying he is done with cigarettes. No single reason, just tired of it. Smoking 8-10/day. Prefers the patch, does not want a pill.

Breathing at baseline. No hemoptysis. Onc infusions continue without trouble.

Exam: vitals as charted, on 2 L. Lungs diminished, scattered end-expiratory wheeze that clears with cough. Heart RRR. Legs in stockings, no edema.

Plan:
- Nicotine patch 21 mg daily starting on his quit day (he picked 3/1). Plan 6 weeks at 21 then step down. Gum not needed per pt.
- Quitline number given. RN to call the week after.
- Again: no smoking anywhere near the oxygen.
- COPD, HTN, warfarin unchanged.

documents.title: Quit check-in
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt one week after his quit date. Patch on daily, mild skin itch where it sits, rotating spots. Has not smoked since 3/1. Cravings worst after dinner, chewing on a straw. Encouraged. No vivid dreams. Will see him for INR on the 22nd.

documents.title: Anticoagulation nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in goal on 5 mg. No bleeding. Three weeks smoke free, proud of it, wife came in too. Reminded that quitting can nudge warfarin levels a bit, which is part of why we are checking. Next in 6 weeks.

documents.title: Electronic refill request
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Pharmacy request: tiotropium capsules 90-day and prednisone 5 mg 90-day. Pulmonology usually writes these but pt asked us to take over refills since he sees us more. PCP approved both, 90-day with 3 refills.

documents.title: Anticoagulation nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. Stepped down to the 14 mg patch two weeks ago, still not smoking. No bleeding or new meds. Continue 5 mg. Next with PCP visit in June.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up letter
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology group, visit of 5/12/2022 (letter received 5/31).

Stage IV NSCLC on pembrolizumab maintenance, now about 18 months from diagnosis. CT chest/abdomen/pelvis 5/5: stable disease, no new lesions. ECOG 1-2, limited mainly by his lungs. He has quit smoking since March, which we applaud. Labs today unremarkable including TSH.

Plan: continue pembrolizumab q3 weeks to complete two years of therapy, anticipated November 2022, then surveillance imaging. Meds and allergies (NKDA) reviewed.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Smoke free since 3/1. Finished the 7 mg patch last week and stopped it; occasional urge, no slips. Cough a little looser if anything. Breathing at his baseline on 2 L, no ED visits. Oncology says stable; immunotherapy to finish in Nov.

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs diminished, no wheeze. RRR. Stockings on; legs without edema.

A/P: Tobacco use disorder in early remission - congratulated. COPD stable. HTN ok. Warfarin, INR today. CMP/CBC today. RTC Sept for wellness visit.

documents.title: Lab review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: CMP, CBC unremarkable. INR in range. Released to portal with a short note.

documents.title: Anticoagulation nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in goal. Heat has kept him indoors. No bleeding. Same dose, 6 weeks.

documents.title: Anticoagulation nurse visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range, 5 mg daily. Small bruise on the forearm from bumping the truck door, otherwise nothing. Wellness visit 9/27.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Initial Medicare AWV.
Functional: independent in ADLs; wife does most driving now; uses a rollator outside and portable O2. No falls this year. Hearing ok. Home has grab bars, rugs taken up.
Mood: PHQ-2 0.
Cognition: clock draw normal, 3/3 recall.
Tobacco: former since 3/2022. Alcohol 1-2/wk.
Advance care: has a health care proxy (wife); discussed goals briefly; wants full treatment for now and will talk with oncology about longer-term wishes.
Screening: colonoscopy 2017 normal; given metastatic cancer, will not pursue further colon screening. No AAA screen needed - he gets CT imaging every 3 months.
Vaccines: Tdap and Shingrix #1 today; #2 in 2-6 mo. Flu with next INR.
Exam: unchanged, lungs diminished, no edema.
Lipids and INR drawn.
Personalized plan printed for him.

documents.title: INR, flu and COVID booster
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in goal, no dose change. High-dose flu R deltoid, bivalent COVID L deltoid. Observed, no reaction. Next INR with his December visit.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Had his last pembrolizumab infusion in November - two years done. Oncology moving to scans every 3 months; keeping the port and flushing it. He is relieved and a bit nervous about being off treatment.
Still not smoking (9 months). Breathing unchanged. Arm sore 2 days after the first shingles shot.

Exam: as before; diminished breath sounds, no edema.
A/P: COPD stable on current regimen. NSCLC off therapy, surveillance per onc. HTN ok. INR today. Shingrix #2 today, series complete. RTC 3-4 mo.
